biography.plain_text: Sir Frederick George Panizzi Preston was a British industrial chairman and Wiltshire landowner. He chaired the engineering manufacturer J. Stone & Co., was appointed KBE in 1918, and served as High Sheriff of Wiltshire in 1921. He later owned Landford Manor, where he supported the parish church, and died in 1949.

confidence.reason: The full identity, 1867-1949 lifespan, J. Stone chairmanship, 1918 KBE, 1921 shrievalty and Landford ownership are independently supported. The wording states only his company role and does not claim that company assets belonged personally to Preston.

long_biography.plain_text:
The engineering enterprise behind Preston's public standing was J. Stone & Co., a Deptford manufacturer with roots in the Victorian period. The firm produced mechanical and electrical equipment for transport and industry, and Preston eventually became chairman. His appointment as a Knight Commander of the Order of the British Empire recognised that work during the First World War.

Landford Manor became the centre of his later life after he bought the Wiltshire estate in 1929. He commissioned new work on the house and reshaped the grounds with formal gardens, woodland walks and a water garden. His patronage extended beyond the estate: he provided St Andrew's church with an organ, acquired the benefice's patronage and donated land for parish use. On his death in 1949, he also left £5,000 to the parochial church council.
